title: A curve with only smooth points and nodes over an algebraically closed field is reduced
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $C$ be a scheme locally of finite type over $F$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose that every closed point $x$ of $C$ [def-weil-closed-points] at which $C\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is not smooth (has no open neighbourhood smooth over $F$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]) has $\mathfrak m_x$-adic completed local ring $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{C,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] isomorphic as a ring to $F[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Then $C$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. No dimension, quasi-compactness, separatedness or properness hypothesis is imposed, and $C$ may be empty.

source.place: Agent statement. Proof plan (for the splitter, not part of the statement): reducedness at smooth closed points from the smooth-fibre reducedness node sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced; at nodes from injectivity of A\to\widehat A, Tag 00MC (algebra-lemma-completion-faithfully-flat), and reducedness of F[[u,v]]/(uv); closed specializations of all points from Jacobson permanence, Tag 00GB (algebra-proposition-Jacobson-permanence). This is the one-field argument of steps 1--3 of lem-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres-reduced, with a ring isomorphism and no hypothesis over larger fields.

proof.text: The field $F$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $F$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth], and [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] applies to the given locally finite type structure morphism to show that $C$ is locally Noetherian. For any $x\in C$, choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ from the Noetherian affine cover in [pqf-def-locnoeth]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $\mathcal O_{C,x}$ is a localization of the Noetherian ring $B$ at the prime of $x$, and is therefore Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. This is a pointwise assertion; no finite cover of $C$ is required.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), locally Noetherian case; properties.tex Tag 01OV (definition-noetherian); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves); algebra.tex Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: Let $x$ be a closed point which has an open neighbourhood $V\subseteq C$ smooth over $F$. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], $V\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ has geometrically reduced fibres. Its fibre over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is $V$ itself, so $V$ is reduced (take the identity field extension). Consequently $\mathcal O_{C,x}=\mathcal O_{V,x}$ is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. The equality of these local rings follows directly from stalks: the neighbourhoods of $x$ contained in the open $V$ are cofinal among all neighbourhoods of $x$.

source.place: Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal), smooth schemes over a field are geometrically reduced; curves.tex Tag 0E37 (lemma-facts-about-nodal-curves), reducedness paragraph. The open-stalk equality is the open-subspace construction, schemes.tex Tag 01HF (example-open-subspace).

proof.text: The model $R=F[[u,v]]/(uv)$ is reduced. Indeed, for the coefficientwise power series of [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], the two axis restrictions define a ring map $F[[u,v]]\to F[[u]]\times F[[v]]$, $f\mapsto(f(u,0),f(0,v))$. Its kernel is exactly $(uv)$: both restrictions vanish precisely when all coefficients with $i=0$ or $j=0$ vanish, and then $f=uvg$ with $g_{ij}=f_{i+1,j+1}$. Thus the induced map from $R$ is injective. Both target factors are domains by [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-domain]. A nilpotent in $R$ maps to zero in each domain and hence is zero by injectivity.

source.place: Tag 0E37 (lemma-facts-about-nodal-curves), final paragraph: the reduced nodal completed local ring; explicit coefficient calculation supplying the assertion for the model ring.

proof.text: Now let $x$ be a closed point having no smooth open neighbourhood. Set $A=\mathcal O_{C,x}$. This is a Noetherian local ring by step 1, so its maximal-ideal completion map $A\to\widehat A$ is faithfully flat by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. In particular it is injective by [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction], with the zero ideal. The hypothesis gives a ring isomorphism $\widehat A\cong R$, where $R$ is reduced by step 3. Any nilpotent of $A$ therefore maps to zero in $R$ and must itself be zero. Together with step 2, this proves reducedness of every local ring at a closed point of $C$. No compatibility of the completed-ring isomorphism with the ground-field maps is used.

source.place: Tags 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat), local-ring clause, and 05CK (lemma-faithfully-flat-universally-injective), injectivity; curves.tex Tag 0E37 (lemma-facts-about-nodal-curves), reducedness argument.

proof.text:
Let $y\in C$. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space], closed points of $C$ in the nonempty closed subset $\overline{\{y\}}$ are dense there. There is therefore such a closed point $x$. Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $x$; it also contains $y$, since every open neighbourhood of a specialization contains its generizations. In the Zariski topology of [def-weil-affine-spectrum], their primes satisfy $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p_y\subseteq\mathfrak p=\mathfrak p_x$ (the closure of $\{\mathfrak q\}$ is $V(\mathfrak q)$). By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], the two local rings are $B_{\mathfrak q}$ and $B_{\mathfrak p}$. The following fraction calculation transfers reducedness, without any global finiteness assumption. If $a/b\in B_{\mathfrak q}$ is nilpotent, take $n\geq1$ and $t
otin\mathfrak q$ with $ta^n=0$, using the zero criterion in [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. In $B_{\mathfrak p}$ one has $(ta/1)^n=0$. This ring is reduced by steps 2 and 4, so $ta/1=0$. The same zero criterion gives $u
otin\mathfrak p$ with $uta=0$. Since $u
otin\mathfrak q$ and $t
otin\mathfrak q$, also $ut
otin\mathfrak q$; hence $a/b=0$ in $B_{\mathfrak q}$. Thus $\mathcal O_{C,y}$ is reduced.

source.place: Tag 0478 (lemma-locally-finite-type-Jacobson), part (2); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), stalk localization; algebra.tex Tag 00CO (definition-localization), fraction equality. The transfer between the two stalks is the displayed elementary fraction calculation.

proof.text: Every local ring of $C$ is reduced by step 5. By [def-pc-reduced-scheme] this says exactly that $C$ is reduced. If $C$ is empty the same local-ring condition is vacuous, so the conclusion includes that case. The proof never restricts the dimension of the smooth open pieces or assumes quasi-compactness, separatedness or properness.
